correctness.rationale: The source quotient field for the seed has transcendence degree one less than its integer-valued-polynomial dimension parameter, and each suspension adds one transcendence variable, giving transcendence degree \(n-1\) for every \(D_{m,n}\). The source inequality \(\dim\operatorname{Int}(D)\le\dim_vD+1\) forces \(\dim_vD_{m,n}\ge n-1\), while every valuation overring has dimension at most the quotient-field transcendence degree, giving equality. Polynomial valuative dimension adds one. The integer-valued polynomial ring has quotient field of transcendence degree \(n\) and ordinary dimension \(n\), so its valuative dimension is \(n\). For \(C_{3,n}\), containment \(D_{3,n}\subseteq C_{3,n}\subseteq\Omega_n\) fixes its quotient field, the source prime chain gives dimension at least \(n-1\), and transcendence degree gives the matching upper bounds for both ordinary and valuative dimension. The localized transform ring is squeezed similarly at dimension \(n\). No finite computation is promoted to an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Valuative dimension is the controlling upper-bound invariant in the dimension problem motivating the source, so computing it exactly for the newly constructed realization family is a natural structural question rather than an arbitrary refinement. The formulas quantify an unbounded Jaffard defect, identify exactly when the polynomial ring recovers Jaffardness, show that the integer-valued polynomial ring always does, and locate the hidden full-dimensional core in the source’s weak coefficient transform. This explains where the dimension inflation is stored in the construction and is useful for comparing future realizations with the same ordinary dimension pairs.
